rule_hypotheses.rule: If covered charges (net of credits) >= Max Benefit, pay exactly Max Benefit (cap). Applies across 2023-2024.

If the PM's net balance is below Max Benefit and consists of damages/cleaning/landscaping/repairs (no excluded fees), the approved amount equals the PM's net claimed balance to the cent (ledger 'Total Unpaid' / statement 'Amount due from resident').

Rent-based cap (rent rounded up to next $500) was NOT enforced in 2023-mid 2024 claims; sheet-wide ~25-30% of posted claims in every half-year exceed it, so the adjuster notes citing it look like retrospective audit comments rather than an applied rule.
Max Benefit = security deposit amount waived on the SD addendum, rounded UP to the next $500 (fee-in-lieu forms without an SD amount appear to use 2x rent).
Agreed Tenant Settlement / Collected Amount (YRIG's recovery from the tenant) does not reduce the Approved Benefit Amount.
PM-side credits (tenant overpayments, rent refunds after re-let, free-rent concessions, post-vacate rent reversals) are netted against charges before paying.
PURE Property Management (SC) adds a $200 Administrative/Maintenance Coordination Fee to every claim with deductions, and it is paid (covered) even though it is an admin-type fee.
Decline (0) when the tenant defaulted on the first full month's rent, regardless of the balance.
Decline when there is no policy on record (Policy # blank on sheet): sheet-wide 33 of 124 Declined claims have blank Policy and 0 of 1100 Posted do.
Test/dummy claims (PM 'Best PM', tenant employer 'YRIG', marketing docs) are Declined/blank -> treat as 0.
Small incidental items (vendor cancellation fee, light bulbs, filters, water-softener salt, dog-feces cleanup bundled in lawn service) are paid without carve-out when the total is under the cap.

extraction_lessons: Blue Fox Properties (AZ) sends a scanned 'Statement of Accounting' form (needs vision): credits block, deduction lines (Unpaid Rent, Lease Break, Cleaning, Repair, Landscaping, Carpet, 'RBP, RIS, 5 day notice and late fees', firm bids, Eviction Costs) and TOTAL DEDUCTIONS; vendor invoices and envelope follow. The total equals the claim; Approved = total when under Max (690) else Max (251).

StarPointe (TX) uses the TAR 'Itemization of Security Deposit' (TXR-2216) form, often scanned and sometimes AMENDED; line (1) damages, line (19) Other can contain negative credits (rent refund), and 'Balance after deductions' in parentheses is the amount owed. It reconciles to the Propertyware ledger 'Total Unpaid'.

Propertyware ledgers (PURE, StarPointe, Blue Fox): use the header 'Balance as of / Total Unpaid'; rows are newest-first with a reverse running balance; 'Unpaid Charge' / 'Partially Paid Charge' rows are the move-out claim; payments may be auto-applied to later damage charges (shows 'Partially Paid') without changing the net balance.

Excalibur Homes (GA) ledgers are statements with TBR-prefixed charges: 'Sec Dep Ins Charge to Tenant' = SDRP premium, 'YRIG Prem', 'Latchel Concierge', 'Eviction Cancellation Fee to Halt Dispo', late charges each month, 'Rent Reservation Fee' charged and reversed (net zero), free-month concessions and a post-vacate rent reversal; damages appear as 'TBR Damages to Property Charges'. The No-Refund letter is boilerplate.
Several folders contain only lease/addendum (165, 681) or a non-claim doc (591): the payout cannot be computed from documents; the Comments sheet sometimes states the claimed total (165: $1,139).

Comments sheet 'Row N' labels do NOT map to sheet row N (tracking N-1): e.g. Hamilton/165 text is at Row 1225, the 690 1366 settlement at Row 55, the Boucouvalas/172 attorney letter at Row 967; match comments by tenant name/amount/date, never by row number.
PURE SC invoices omit the lease's $200 Maintenance Coordination fee; the PM's claim (and payout) includes it - add 200 for PURE SC claims when only a vendor invoice is present.
Firm bids/estimates (work not yet done) are included in PM totals and appear to be accepted.
Max Benefit can be cross-checked from the SD waiver addendum (SD amount rounded up to $500).
